title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Association Contract

scope.purpose: Define how an Observation Unit instance is associated with a Step-owned observation target scope, how that association is identified and governed, and how its historical identity is preserved.
scope.appliesTo: Each concrete Step specialization that associates an Observation Unit instance with one or more internal target scopes.

definition.association: An explicit Step-owned relationship that makes a particular Observation Unit instance applicable to observe a particular Step-owned target scope under a defined specialization.
associationIsNot: Ownership of the Observation Unit instance by the target.
Transfer of association-management authority to the Observation Unit or target SPU.
An observation invocation, observation record, or observation destination.
A guarantee that observation is currently active or that the Unit is lifecycle-ready.
A guarantee that every event or fact about the target will be observed.

identities.stepInstanceIdentity: Identifies the owning Step instance within which the association exists.
identities.observationUnitIdentity: Identifies the concrete Observation Unit runtime instance participating in the association.
identities.associationTargetIdentity: Identifies the Step-owned target scope to which the Observation Unit is applicable.
identities.observationUnitAssociationIdentity: Identifies one particular relationship between one Observation Unit instance and one target scope within one Step instance.

permittedKinds: A specific SPU instance or SPU-defined observation scope.
The owning Step instance as a whole.
Another explicitly identified internal Step scope, operation, execution context, or component boundary defined by the concrete Step.
rules: The common contract does not assume that an Observation Unit is associated only with an SPU.
The target scope must be identifiable independently of the Observation Unit instance and association.
A target may expose an observation surface, events, state, or context without transferring ownership or orchestration authority to the Observation Unit.
The concrete Step defines the target identity representation and the exact observation-relevant boundary.
associationTargetIdentity must distinguish the target scope kind and the concrete target instance within the owning Step.

permitted: One Observation Unit instance may have multiple associations to distinct target scopes where the concrete Step permits it.
Multiple Observation Unit instances may be associated with the same target where the concrete Step permits it.
notMandated: Exclusivity of an instance or target.
A universal cardinality or association limit.
multiplicity.identityRule: Each association is a separately identifiable relationship, even when the instance or target is shared.

authorityAndOwnership.authority: The owning Step Composition is authoritative for creating, activating, changing, rebinding, deactivating where applicable, and ending Observation Unit Associations.
rules: Association creation and changes are Step-specific composition decisions.
An Observation Unit may use an association context supplied to it but cannot create, mutate, select a replacement for, or terminate that association.
An SPU may be an association target but does not thereby gain association-management authority.
Association authority remains with Step Composition even if the Observation Unit is implemented as a callback registered with the target or as a subscriber to a target event source.
Association does not by itself transfer ownership of target resources, event sources, subscriptions, or observation destinations; each resource owner is defined separately.
separation: Association existence is distinct from instance readiness/admission under the Lifecycle Contract.
Association existence is distinct from an active observation activity or subscription.
Association termination is distinct from instance release.
Association metadata retention is distinct from observation record retention.

preconditions: The Observation Unit instance is known to the owning Step Composition and has a stable observationUnitIdentity.
The target scope is known and has an associationTargetIdentity within the owning Step instance.
The instance satisfies the Lifecycle Contract conditions required for association establishment by the concrete specialization.
The Step specialization defines the capability/target compatibility required for this association.
establishment: Step Composition creates a distinct observationUnitAssociationIdentity for the relationship.
The association records the stepInstanceIdentity, observationUnitIdentity, and associationTargetIdentity binding.
Step Composition establishes specialization-defined target observation surfaces, callback registrations, subscriptions, or access arrangements without transferring association authority.
The association becomes usable for new observation activity only when its concrete establishment/activation conditions are satisfied.
associationEstablishment.activationBoundary: The common contract does not require association creation to activate observation immediately. The concrete Step may establish an association before an observation activity is enabled and may define explicit activation/deactivation semantics.

invocationBinding.rule: Every observation activity performed under an association is correlated with exactly one observationUnitAssociationIdentity and the corresponding associationTargetIdentity.
constraints: An Observation Unit instance with multiple associations must receive or resolve an explicit association context for each activity.
The target identity used for an activity must match the target bound to the selected association.
An activity already authorized under an association is not silently redirected if the association changes or ends while work is in progress.

The concrete Step defines whether an active subscription/callback is bound to one association for its full activation lifetime or whether each delivered event carries a separately resolved association context; either model must preserve unambiguous provenance.
Observation records retain the association identity historically after the association ends.

rules: A change in target scope or applicability is represented by an explicit Step Composition-managed association change, not by silently mutating historical identity.

If a change alters the identity of the target relationship, the concrete Step should end the old association and establish a new association identity unless its specialization explicitly defines a safe in-place change with equivalent provenance guarantees.
An observation activity already in progress remains attributable to the association under which it was authorized.
The concrete Step defines how target-side registrations, callbacks, subscriptions, and handles are updated and reconciled.
noImplicitEffects: Changing an association does not automatically create, release, or replace an Observation Unit instance.
Changing an association does not delete or rewrite already emitted observation records.
Changing an association does not decide whether pending observation records are delivered, retained, or recovered.

dissociation.authority: Step Composition exclusively coordinates and authorizes association termination.
rules: Dissociation ends the association's authority to authorize new observation activities.
Dissociation does not imply Observation Unit instance release or shutdown.
Dissociation does not automatically cancel or erase records already produced or accepted.
The concrete Step defines how active subscriptions, callbacks, queued events, and in-flight observation activities are stopped or reconciled.
The concrete Step defines whether an in-flight activity may complete under its original association after dissociation begins; any such completion retains the original association provenance.
The association identity remains historically interpretable for as long as retained observations or other evidence refer to it.
Dissociation does not invalidate historical observation records produced under the association.
Retaining association metadata does not require retaining the Observation Unit runtime instance, target runtime object, callback, subscription handle, or other resource.
Historical association identity must not be reused in a way that makes prior records ambiguous.
The concrete Step defines metadata retention sufficient to interpret historical records and audit their association provenance.

required: Define concrete identity representation and uniqueness scope for Step, Observation Unit, target, and association identities.
Define permitted target kinds and observation-relevant scope boundaries.
Define allowed multiplicity and whether one instance may observe multiple targets or multiple instances may observe one target.
Define compatibility rules between the Observation Unit capability and target scope.
Define establishment, activation, deactivation, change, and dissociation mechanics.
Define ownership and release of callbacks, event subscriptions, target access surfaces, and other association resources.
Define in-flight activity and queued-event behavior during association change or dissociation.
Define historical association metadata retention and correlation with observation records.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A concrete association specialization is complete when target scope, identity, multiplicity, authority, activation, change/dissociation, in-flight activity, and historical provenance rules are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No universal cardinality, exclusivity, or one-to-one mapping.
No ownership transfer from Step Composition to Observation Unit or target SPU.
No automatic instance creation, admission, release, or result retention caused solely by association changes.
No mandatory subscription, callback, event bus, registry, or central association manager.
No universal observation trigger, event ordering, or delivery guarantee.

references.relationship: Behavior performed under an established association and observation-result provenance.
Instance readiness and lifecycle preconditions for association establishment and use.
Step Composition authority over internal association and lifecycle coordination.
Step aggregate boundary and internal component association.
Supporting-unit target scope may be SPU, Step, or another Step-defined internal scope.
Framework-level association coordination invariants refined by this specialized Association Contract; specialized identity names and behavior remain authoritative.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.

frameworkIdentityRoleMapping.targetIdentitySemantics: associationTargetIdentity identifies both the target scope kind and the concrete target instance within the owning Step; it must not be represented by a bare SPU identity when the target scope may instead be Step-wide or another Step-internal scope.
